class: cheap experiment settled a design question
what_happened: A 5-line flock experiment showed a child that re-opens the lock file blocks against its lock-holding parent while an inherited fd does not; this fixes the rule that the lock is taken at exactly one level of a script call chain.

class: cheap experiment settled a design question
what_happened: Plan verification designed around a stub lake on PATH: exercises lock wait, timeout and post-acquire control flow for all four changed scripts with no build and no write to typst/generated/status.typ, which sibling task 803 owns this cycle.

validate-artifact.sh flagged a Tier Justification built from per-path suite_selection_select calls: the selector returns __FULL_SWEEP__ for a path SET when any member is unmapped, so per-path output (typst-sync-check.sh -> test-plan-file-scope-harvest.sh) is not the phase-level answer. Fixed by re-running the selector over the phase's full path list.
A stub lake on PATH plus a bounded flock holder exercised every lock, timeout and post-acquisition branch in four scripts without starting a real build or writing any generated file.

Two held-lock test runs used a holder that expired before the command under test finished (the build-free modes take 10-20s), so the first timeout-branch run fell through to the stub; both were re-run with a longer bounded hold and then passed.
run_dataset_generation.sh prebuild was gated to generation commands so help and an unknown command do not trigger a build; the plan placed it unconditionally after check_prereqs.

The task description's two lead candidates were mis-shaped (typst-module-map.sh never invokes lake; export-training-data.sh's lake build is an echoed hint); the independent sweep also surfaced warning-budget.py, .githooks/pre-commit and two non-script files absent from the description's list, each given its own determination in scripts/README.md.
